Big Ten Women's Basketball · Love Data Week 2027

Maize, Blue, and a Fuller Big Ten

The Caitlin Clark years filled Big Ten arenas. Two seasons later: which crowds stayed, how far the conference now travels, and where Michigan stands.

3,532 → 5,334average fans per Big Ten home game, 2021–22 to 2025–26
1,600,066fans at 300 Big Ten home games in 2025–26 (vs. 766,393 at 217 in 2021–22)
2.9×more conference road miles after the 2024 expansion
Chapter 1 · The wave

Iowa drew crowds everywhere it went, then the wave passed

In 2021–22, a Big Ten home game against Iowa drew about 3,907 fans. Two seasons later, with Caitlin Clark chasing the NCAA scoring record, the same road games averaged 13,963. When she left for the WNBA, Iowa's road crowds fell back to about 5,600. Iowa's home crowds did not fall: Carver-Hawkeye Arena still averaged 14,918 in 2025–26.

The quieter line matters most. Big Ten home games not involving Iowa rose from 3,096 to 4,728 fans per game, and they kept most of that gain after the peak.

Average reported attendance at Big Ten conference-member home games, by season. Hover for the number of games behind each point; click a legend item to isolate a series. Neutral-site games are excluded.

Chapter 2 · The baseline

Thirteen seasons of crowds, school by school

Read across a row to follow one program. Iowa's row darkens first and most. Indiana and Maryland follow. The right-hand columns are darker than 2021–22 for 13 of the 14 schools that were members in both seasons.

Each cell is one team's average reported home attendance in one season. Blank cells mean the school was not yet a Big Ten member. The 2020–21 season is omitted because most crowds were restricted for COVID-19.

Who kept the fans?

Comparing each program's 2025–26 average with its 2021–22 average shows who turned the boom into lasting growth. Illinois grew the most, from about 1,240 to 5,770 per game (4.7×). Penn State is the only school whose average fell (0.87×).

Ratio of mean home attendance, 2025–26 ÷ 2021–22. 1× means no change. Includes the 14 schools that were members in both seasons.

Chapter 3 · The map

The conference got a lot wider

In 2024–25, UCLA, USC, Oregon, and Washington joined the Big Ten. Summed over every conference road trip, the league's one-way travel went from about 50,841 miles in 2023–24 to 147,780 in 2025–26. Switch seasons to see the gold lines appear.

Lines join campuses that met in regular-season conference play. Hover a line for the straight-line distance and the number of games.

Sum of straight-line, one-way, campus-to-campus distance for each conference road game (true travel distance is longer). Michigan's total roughly doubled, from 2,846 to 5,760 miles. UCLA now covers about 14,383.

Chapter 4 · Home

Meanwhile in Ann Arbor

Michigan's crowds grew more slowly than many rivals' (1.3×). Even so, Crisler Center averaged 4,770 fans in 2025–26, Michigan's highest season average in this record (the previous best was 4,140 in 2022–23). On the court, the Wolverines scored 82.3 points per game, their highest since at least 2011–12 and well above the Big Ten average of 74.7. They won 28 of 35 games.

Points per game across all games in the data (regular season and postseason). The Big Ten average is the mean across all games played by conference members. 2020–21 is omitted.

Data integrity

How the numbers were checked

One crowd that didn't happen. The source data lists 111,368 fans at Breslin Center for Michigan at Michigan State on Feb. 24, 2019. Breslin seats about 15,000. This value is almost certainly a typing error (one extra digit), so the game is excluded. Left in, it would have inflated Michigan State's 2018–19 home average from 5,105 to 11,746.

What this shows and doesn't. These charts describe patterns in reported attendance. They do not prove that any one player caused them: TV deals, ticket pricing, scheduling, and team success all play a part. Attendance figures are as reported by schools to ESPN. Conference membership is taken season by season from the data, so Nebraska is counted from 2011–12, Maryland and Rutgers from 2014–15, and the four West Coast schools from 2024–25. Travel distances use approximate campus coordinates and great-circle distance.

Data: NCAA women's college basketball schedules and team box scores from ESPN, compiled by the SportsDataverse wehoop project (the source of the BTAA 2027 Love Data Week dataset). Basemap: U.S. Census-derived TopoJSON from vega-datasets. Built with Vega-Lite.
